iPhone version is atrocious. Android is better.. I cannot believe that you believe people typing do not make errors. We are all imperfect. Apps should be created around this concept. When typing sentences to be translated and one makes an error, and wishes to browse slightly to make the correction, the slightest move from your finger will make your entire paragraph disappear forever !!! There is no automatic cache to save it. Before making corrections one must hit save, copy, and then return to the original clean translation screen, paste, then make their corrections. I do not know another translator app where this occurs. The reason for the 2-star, and not a 1 star is because the translations are pretty accurate. More accurate than even Google Translate on most occasions. If your Android version works almost seamlessly, then why have iPhone work as seamlessly? Lastly, it appears the iPhone version also does not have the multi-person conversation microphones so two people can converse smoothly in-sync.

reviews.text: This is a phenomenal app!. I use this app with my patients and families when finding someone is near impossible for interpreting. It has so many languages and is free! I couldn’t eat it high enough ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ and recommend it to anyone needing 1 app for any potential language barrier. It also saves the conversations so you’re able to view later, or if people have a hard time hearing the verbal translation they can read, type etc. It’s perfect and I’ve tried other apps, google translate - this beats them all!

Best translator by far. And FREE. So easy to use. And accurate so far. But this app is ridiculously hard to find in the App Store, in spite of its great ratings. When checking in at a hotel, the reception used it (in Vietnamese) I was blown away with the way it worked, and went searching for “translator” in the App Store. After installing several expensive look alikes, and scrolling through countless pages of apps, this one did not show up. In the end I had to photograph the guys iPhone showing the icon for the app and do a Google image search to find it. It should not be that hard. (I’m blaming Apple for that though)
